newsitem.title: USA: California foreclosures surged in 1996 - report.
newsitem.headline: California foreclosures surged in 1996 - report.

text.p: Financial institutions foreclosed on more than 92,000 California properties with a combined mortgage value of $13.8 billion in 1996, an increase of 19 percent from 1995, according to a report on Tuesday.
Foreclosure levels are now six times higher than in 1989, Experian, which monitors the real estate market, said in its year end report on foreclosures in California.

"The recent rise in property repossessions could well be reflective of lenders' willingness to foreclose on delinquent loans more swiftly than before, but it is also a symptom of deteriorating quality of mortgages being originated," Nima Nattagh, Experian's market analyst, said in a statement.
Experian estimated that there are 477,000 California homeowners with negative equity brought on by a combination of low down payment mortgages and declining values.

Real estate foreclosures in California have been increasing at double digit rates since 1991 when the state's economic recession set in motion a wave of property repossessions and declines in home values, Experian said.
